raw.Connection Title: Pemphigus vulgaris clinical and biopsy clues
raw.Explanation: Pemphigus vulgaris combines fragile intraepidermal blisters and frequent mucosal disease with keratinocyte separation and a net-like intercellular IgG pattern.
raw.Source Section: Autoimmune Blistering Conditions > Pemphigus Vulgaris and Summary, PDF pp. 73, 76
raw.Notes: Verified: suprabasal acantholysis, fishnet/intercellular IgG on DIF, anti-desmoglein 3 +/- 1. Added refs: Schmidt E et al, Lancet 2019; Kasperkiewicz M et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2017.

raw.Explanation: Dermatitis herpetiformis is linked to celiac disease and intensely itchy extensor lesions, with granular IgA at dermal papillae; dapsone can control the skin eruption.

raw.Notes: Verified: cutaneous manifestation of celiac disease; pathognomonic granular IgA in dermal papillae; skin autoantigen is epidermal transglutaminase (TG3) vs intestinal tTG (TG2). raw.Explanation: DRESS refers to a delayed drug reaction with an exanthem, eosinophilia, and systemic manifestations. The group describes a characteristic syndrome rather than mandatory findings at every time point.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms; DRESS features

raw.Notes: Verified: latency 2-8 weeks, morbilliform eruption (near-universal), eosinophilia (~52-95%, time-variable), multiorgan involvement (liver most common). raw.Notes: Verified type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity pathway plus its histologic consequence (spongiosis). raw.Explanation: The source identifies these settings as associated with cutaneous SCC. Chronic wounds and burn scars represent persistent local injury contexts; exposure and immune status provide additional risk pathways.

raw.Notes: Verified: dome-shaped, central keratin plug, rapid growth over 4-6 weeks, possible (not inevitable) regression. Added refs: Tisack A et al, Br J Dermatol 2021; Nagarajan P, J Cutan Pathol 2020.

raw.Explanation: Glomus tumors arise from the glomus body and classically present as a painful, cold-sensitive, red-blue subungual nodule; the triad of paroxysmal pain, pinpoint tenderness (Love test), and cold hypersensitivity is characteristic.

raw.Explanation: Bacillary angiomatosis is linked to Bartonella and vascular skin lesions, with bacteria demonstrable by a silver stain and a neutrophil-rich inflammatory component.
raw.Source Section: Vascular Tumors > Bacillary Angiomatosis, PDF p. 112
raw.Notes: Verified (B. henselae/quintana; lobular vascular proliferation with neutrophils around bacterial aggregates; Warthin-Starry positive). Neutrophilic infiltrate is frequent but variable; Warthin-Starry is not specific/always positive. Clinically mimics pyogenic granuloma and Kaposi sarcoma. Added refs: Adal KA et al, N Engl J Med 1994; Cockerell CJ, LeBoit PE, J Am Acad Dermatol 1990.

raw.Explanation: Kaposi sarcoma is associated with HHV-8, purple lesions, and spindle-cell histology. HIV-associated immune dysfunction is an important risk context rather than a universal feature.
raw.Source Section: Vascular Tumors > Kaposi Sarcoma, PDF p. 113
raw.Notes: Verified: HHV-8/KSHV is etiologic in all forms; CD31/CD34/LANA-positive spindle cells; HIV elevates risk up to ~20,000-fold but KS also occurs in classic/endemic/iatrogenic forms. HHV-8 and HIV play distinct roles and are not interchangeable causes. Added refs: Cesarman E et al, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2019; Yarchoan R, Uldrick TS, N Engl J Med 2018; Li JJ et al, Am J Pathol 1996.

raw.Explanation: Acanthosis nigricans produces velvety hyperpigmented plaques, often in folds. It is commonly linked to insulin resistance, while an abrupt presentation can raise concern for a malignant association.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Acanthosis nigricans; Benign and malignant acanthosis nigricans associations
raw.Source Section: Benign Dark Skin Lesions > Acanthosis Nigricans, PDF p. 117
raw.Notes: Verified: insulin resistance (benign, common) and malignant AN (abrupt, ~60% gastric adenocarcinoma, TGF-alpha/EGFR driven) are distinct contexts, not features required together. Most cases are benign -- do not imply most signal cancer. Board-overlap warning: shares a paraneoplastic/gastric-cancer axis with DERM-038 (Leser-Trelat); the two frequently co-occur. Added refs: Valejo Coelho MM et al, JAMA Dermatol 2019; Gillespie J et al, Am J Clin Dermatol 2026.

raw.Explanation: The source describes seborrheic keratoses as benign, often pigmented lesions with an adherent appearance that become more common with age. Abrupt eruption of numerous lesions is described as the Leser-Trelat sign.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Seborrheic keratosis; SK appearance and eruptive pattern
raw.Source Section: Benign Dark Skin Lesions > Seborrheic Keratosis, PDF p. 118
raw.Notes: Verified morphology and eruptive Leser-Trelat concept (classically gastric/GI adenocarcinoma). Added refs: Schwartz RA, J Am Acad Dermatol 1996; Husain Z et al, J Drugs Dermatol 2013; Lindelof B et al, J Am Acad Dermatol 1992.

raw.Connection Title: Hypothalamic hormones that stimulate anterior pituitary secretion
raw.Explanation: TRH stimulates TSH secretion; GnRH stimulates LH and FSH; CRH stimulates ACTH; GHRH stimulates GH. These are hypothalamic releasing signals.

raw.Source Section: Hypothalamus: Function, p. 7; Anterior Pituitary: Function, p. 16
raw.Notes: Verified stimulatory (releasing) hormones; dopamine and somatostatin are the inhibitory counterparts and are correct distractors. Ref: Molina PE, Endocrine Physiology 5e (McGraw Hill); Van Uytfanghe K et al., Thyroid 2023.

raw.Connection Title: Anterior pituitary hormones targeting other endocrine glands
raw.Explanation: TSH acts on the thyroid, ACTH on the adrenal cortex, and FSH and LH on gonadal endocrine function.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Tropic anterior pituitary hormones; Pituitary gland-to-gland signals
raw.Source Section: Anterior Pituitary: Function, p. 16
raw.Notes: Tropic hormones acting on downstream endocrine glands; GH and prolactin are correct non-tropic distractors. ACTH is a peptide, so a 'glycoprotein hormones' label would wrongly exclude it. Board overlap: avoid pairing with a separate glycoprotein-hormone (TSH/FSH/LH/hCG) set. Ref: Molina PE, Endocrine Physiology 5e.

raw.Connection Title: Acquired causes of central diabetes insipidus
raw.Explanation: These processes can injure the hypothalamic-neurohypophyseal system and reduce effective ADH secretion, producing central diabetes insipidus.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Causes of ADH deficiency; Causes of central DI
raw.Source Section: Diabetes Insipidus: Pathophysiology, p. 10
raw.Notes: TBI, SAH, meningitis, and Langerhans cell histiocytosis are established acquired causes of central DI; not inevitable. Ref: Refardt J et al. Clin Endocrinol 2019; Driano JE et al. Pediatrics 2021 (DI vs SIADH).

raw.Connection Title: Dopamine-blocking drugs that can elevate prolactin
raw.Explanation: Dopamine normally suppresses lactotroph secretion. Blocking dopamine receptors can remove that inhibition and cause hyperprolactinemia.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: D2 antagonists causing hyperprolactinemia; Drug-induced prolactin elevation
raw.Source Section: Hyperprolactinemia: Pathophysiology, p. 20
raw.Notes: Risperidone, haloperidol, fluphenazine (antipsychotic D2 antagonists) and metoclopramide (prokinetic D2 antagonist) cause hyperprolactinemia by disinhibition; metoclopramide prevents an 'all-antipsychotic' reading. Ref: Katzung Basic & Clinical Pharmacology 15e.

raw.Connection Title: Drugs that reduce peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion
raw.Explanation: The source lists PTU, beta blockers, glucocorticoids and amiodarone as inhibitors of peripheral thyroid hormone conversion. Propranolol is the beta blocker named elsewhere in the thyroid section.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Peripheral deiodination inhibitors; Drugs inhibiting T4 activation
raw.Source Section: T3, T4 Synthesis and Pharmacology, p. 25; Graves Disease: Management, p. 26
raw.Notes: Confirmed inhibitors of peripheral T4-to-T3 (type I 5'-deiodinase): PTU, glucocorticoids, amiodarone, and propranolol. QUALIFIER: propranolol inhibits conversion only at high dose (>160 mg/day) and the effect is not clinically relevant at usual doses; do not generalize to all beta-blockers. Ref: Burch HB. Drug Effects on the Thyroid. NEJM 2019; Van Uytfanghe K et al. Thyroid 2023; FDA levothyroxine label.

raw.Connection Title: Components of the source thyroid-storm regimen
raw.Explanation: The source four-part regimen combines adrenergic control, a thionamide, a glucocorticoid and iodine. This is a regimen association, not a shared mechanism.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Four Ps of thyroid storm; Source-listed thyroid storm therapies
raw.Source Section: Graves Disease: Complications, p. 26
raw.Notes: ATA-supported thyroid-storm regimen: thionamide (PTU) + beta-blocker (propranolol) + glucocorticoid + iodide (KI). CRITICAL QUALIFIER: iodide must be given >=1 h AFTER the thionamide; not simultaneous or a universally required set. ATA names hydrocortisone or dexamethasone as the glucocorticoid, so 'prednisolone' is a defensible but non-canonical substitute. Ref: Ross DS et al. ATA 2016 Hyperthyroidism Guidelines, Thyroid; Wiersinga WM et al. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2023.

raw.Connection Title: Antibody and histology clues to Hashimoto thyroiditis
raw.Explanation: Hashimoto thyroiditis is associated with thyroid autoantibodies, oncocytic follicular-cell changes and lymphoid aggregates with germinal centers.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Hashimoto thyroiditis findings; Chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis
raw.Source Section: Hyper/Hypothyroidism: Thyroiditis, pp. 28-29
raw.Notes: Anti-TPO, anti-Tg, Hurthle (oncocytic) cells, and germinal-center lymphoid follicles are characteristic of Hashimoto; none is individually specific, so 'autoimmune thyroiditis' is acceptable only with a compatible explanation. Ref: Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease 10e.

raw.Connection Title: Molecular and microscopic clues to papillary thyroid carcinoma
raw.Explanation: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is associated with characteristic nuclear clearing, calcified psammoma bodies and the listed oncogenic alterations.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Papillary thyroid cancer associations; Papillary carcinoma clues

raw.Connection Title: Calcium-raising and phosphate-lowering actions of PTH
raw.Explanation: PTH conserves renal calcium, promotes phosphaturia, stimulates calcitriol formation and indirectly increases osteoclast-mediated resorption through osteoblast-lineage cells.
raw.Source Section: Parathyroid Location and Function, p. 35
raw.Notes: Distal tubular Ca reabsorption, phosphaturia, renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase induction, and (indirect, RANKL-mediated via osteoblast-lineage cells) osteoclastic resorption are core PTH actions; resorption assumes sustained PTH signaling and is not direct on osteoclasts. Ref: Walker MD, Silverberg SJ. Nat Rev Endocrinol 2018; Guyton & Hall 14e.

raw.Connection Title: Malabsorptive settings that predispose to vitamin D deficiency

raw.Notes: Celiac, cystic fibrosis, IBD, and gastric bypass impair absorption of fat-soluble vitamin D; malabsorption is not universal in all IBD or after every bypass, so 'predispose' wording is appropriate. Ref: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 14e.

raw.Connection Title: Typical laboratory tendencies in primary hyperparathyroidism
raw.Explanation: Autonomous PTH secretion can raise calcium, promote phosphate loss and increase bone turnover with alkaline phosphatase elevation.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Primary hyperparathyroidism laboratory profile; PTH-driven hypercalcemia
raw.Source Section: Hyperparathyroidism: Primary, p. 38
raw.Notes: High Ca, high or inappropriately-normal PTH, and low phosphate are typical of primary HPT; ALP is often NORMAL in mild disease and PTH may be inappropriately normal rather than frankly elevated - this is a 'typical profile', not diagnostic criteria. Ref: Walker MD, Silverberg SJ. Nat Rev Endocrinol 2018; Bilezikian JP et al. Lancet 2018; Insogna KL. NEJM 2018.

raw.Connection Title: Laboratory pattern of CKD-related secondary hyperparathyroidism
raw.Explanation: Impaired renal phosphate excretion and calcitriol generation can lower calcium and stimulate secondary PTH secretion in CKD.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Renal secondary hyperparathyroidism; CKD mineral metabolism changes
raw.Source Section: Hyperparathyroidism: Secondary, p. 38
raw.Notes: Phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol drive low/low-normal Ca and elevated PTH in CKD; values vary with CKD stage and therapy, so the low-normal calcium qualifier avoids making hypocalcemia universal. Ref: KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD Guideline; Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 14e.

raw.Connection Title: Laboratory clues to untreated primary adrenal insufficiency
raw.Explanation: Adrenal failure lowers cortisol and mineralocorticoid output. Loss of cortisol feedback raises ACTH; mineralocorticoid deficiency can impair potassium excretion.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Addison disease laboratory clues; Primary adrenal failure
raw.Source Section: Primary Adrenal Insufficiency: Diagnostics, p. 44
raw.Notes: High ACTH, low cortisol, low aldosterone, and hyperkalemia characterize untreated primary AI; hyperkalemia is present in only ~50% at diagnosis, and preserved aldosterone distinguishes secondary/tertiary AI. Ref: Vaidya A et al. Adrenal Insufficiency. JAMA 2025; Husebye ES et al. J Intern Med 2014; Bornstein SR et al. Endocrine Society 2016.

raw.Connection Title: Characteristic physical findings of Cushing syndrome
raw.Explanation: Excess glucocorticoid effect produces skin and connective-tissue changes and altered fat distribution, including these findings.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Cushingoid appearance; Physical findings of glucocorticoid excess
raw.Source Section: Hypercortisolism: Presentation, p. 47
raw.Notes: Purple striae, thin skin, central adiposity, and dorsocervical fat pad reflect glucocorticoid excess and also fit chronic exogenous steroid effect; do not label 'Cushing disease' (pituitary-source-specific). Ref: Nieman LK et al. Endocrine Society Cushing Guideline, JCEM 2008.

raw.Connection Title: Molecular and diagnostic associations of neuroblastoma
raw.Explanation: Neuroblastoma can show MYCN amplification, increased catecholamine metabolites in urine and neuroblastic rosettes on microscopy.
raw.Source Section: Adrenal Neoplasms: Neuroblastoma, p. 50
raw.Notes: MYCN amplification (prognostic subset, not universal), urinary VMA and HVA (distinct catecholamine metabolites), and Homer-Wright rosettes characterize neuroblastoma; rosettes also occur in other neural tumors. Ref: Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics 21e; Robbins & Cotran 10e.

raw.Connection Title: Recessive enzyme defects affecting sex-steroid synthesis or activation
raw.Explanation: The source groups these inherited enzyme defects when evaluating differences in sex development and describes each as autosomal recessive. They affect androgen synthesis or androgen activation.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Autosomal recessive steroid enzyme deficiencies; Recessive defects of androgen synthesis or activation
raw.Source Section: Adrenal Cortex Pathways Overview and Enzyme Deficiencies, pp. 51-56
raw.Notes: All four are autosomal recessive enzyme deficiencies of sex-steroid synthesis (21-OH, 17-alpha-OH, 11-beta-OH) or androgen activation (5-alpha-reductase). CRITICAL: 5-alpha-reductase deficiency is NOT a form of CAH - never accept an 'all are CAH' label. Shared autosomal recessive inheritance is the clean unifying category. Ref: El-Maouche D et al. CAH, Lancet 2017; Thigpen AE et al. NEJM 1992; MedlinePlus '5-alpha reductase deficiency'.

raw.Connection Title: Steroid and electrolyte pattern of 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency
raw.Explanation: Impaired 17-alpha-hydroxylation reduces sex-steroid synthesis while increasing mineralocorticoid-active precursors, producing hypertension and potassium loss.

raw.Connection Title: Clues to 5-alpha-reductase deficiency in a 46,XY patient
raw.Explanation: Reduced conversion of testosterone to DHT impairs DHT-dependent external development while preserving testosterone-dependent internal structures. Pubertal testosterone increases can cause virilization.
raw.Source Section: 5-alpha-reductase Deficiency, p. 55
raw.Notes: 5-alpha-reductase type 2 deficiency (46,XY): reduced DHT, elevated T:DHT ratio, preserved testosterone-dependent Wolffian internal structures, pubertal virilization; the 46,XY qualifier is essential and 'internal structures' means T-dependent male ducts. Ref: Thigpen AE et al. NEJM 1992; Reyes AP et al. Nat Rev Urol 2023; MedlinePlus.

raw.Connection Title: Renal pathologic findings of diabetic nephropathy
raw.Explanation: Chronic diabetic injury can thicken the glomerular basement membrane, scar glomeruli and produce hyaline deposition in both afferent and efferent arterioles.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Diabetic nephropathy pathology; Diabetic renal microvascular injury
raw.Source Section: Diabetic Complications: Non-enzymatic Glycation, p. 64
raw.Notes: GBM thickening, (Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodular) glomerulosclerosis, and hyalinosis of BOTH afferent and efferent arterioles characterize diabetic nephropathy; efferent arteriolar involvement helps distinguish it from hypertensive nephrosclerosis (afferent-predominant). Not all lesions in every patient. Ref: Robbins & Cotran 10e.

raw.Connection Title: Sulfonylureas that stimulate insulin release via KATP-channel closure
raw.Explanation: These sulfonylureas close beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channels, causing depolarization and calcium-dependent insulin secretion.
raw.Source Section: Diabetes Type 2: Management - Sulfonylureas, p. 68
raw.Notes: Tolbutamide (1st-generation), glipizide, glyburide, glimepiride (2nd-generation) are sulfonylureas that close beta-cell K-ATP channels -> depolarization and insulin secretion; do not label 'all second-generation'. raw.Connection Title: Source-listed glucose-lowering agents associated with weight loss
raw.Explanation: The source associates metformin, SGLT2 inhibition and the two named GLP1 agonists with weight loss. These effects differ in magnitude and are not guaranteed.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Diabetes medications associated with weight loss; Weight-reducing antihyperglycemic drugs
raw.Source Section: Diabetes Type 2: Management, p. 68
raw.Notes: Metformin (weight-neutral to modest ~2-3% loss), SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin), and GLP-1 agonists (exenatide, liraglutide) are associated with weight loss; magnitude GLP-1 > SGLT2 > metformin. 'Associated with', not guaranteed; metformin may be weight-neutral. Ref: Davies MJ et al. ADA/EASD 2022, Diabetologia; Tsapas A et al. Diabetes Obes Metab 2021 (network meta-analysis).

content.notes: Metformin (weight-neutral to modest ~2-3% loss), SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin), and GLP-1 agonists (exenatide, liraglutide) are associated with weight loss; magnitude GLP-1 > SGLT2 > metformin. raw.Connection Title: Physiologic inhibitors of gastric acid secretion
raw.Explanation: Somatostatin is the principal physiologic inhibitor of gastric acid; secretin inhibits acid via somatostatin and prostaglandin release; cholecystokinin inhibits acid largely by stimulating somatostatin; prostaglandin E2 directly inhibits parietal cells (EP3/Gi). The original GIP tile was replaced because GIP inhibits acid only at supraphysiologic doses and is not a physiologic inhibitor in humans.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Enterogastrones; Physiologic inhibitors of gastric H+ secretion
raw.Source Section: Stomach / Gastric Regulation; Intestinal Regulation; Parietal Cell Physiology; PDF pp. 36, 38-39
raw.Notes: REVISED: GIP replaced by cholecystokinin. GIP acid inhibition is a pharmacologic artifact (name changed from gastric inhibitory to glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide). Added refs: Baggio & Drucker, Gastroenterology 2007; Nauck et al., Digestion 1992; Meier et al., World J Gastroenterol 2006; Schubert & Rehfeld, Compr Physiol 2019; Chung et al., Gastroenterology 1994. Board overlap: shares secretin and CCK with GI-012; do not use both on one board.

raw.Connection Title: Intestinal hormones that slow gastric emptying
raw.Explanation: Secretin, CCK, peptide YY, and GLP-1 are intestinal ('ileal brake') hormones that slow gastric emptying, coordinating delivery of chyme with intestinal digestive capacity. The original GIP tile was replaced because controlled human studies show GIP does not slow gastric emptying and may slightly accelerate it.

raw.Connection Title: Gastrointestinal causes of vitamin B12 deficiency
raw.Explanation: Each can cause B12 deficiency by a distinct GI mechanism: loss of intrinsic factor (pernicious anemia), failure to cleave R-protein-B12 (pancreatic insufficiency), mucosal malabsorption +/- concomitant autoimmune gastritis (celiac disease), and luminal competition (D. latum).
raw.Source Section: Stomach / Pernicious Anemia; PDF pp. 40
raw.Notes: Preserve can cause wording. Celiac-related B12 deficiency is legitimate but less characteristic than iron/folate (terminal ileum relatively spared). Verified: Green et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers 2017; Stabler, NEJM 2013; Allen et al., J Clin Invest 1978; Oxentenko & Murray, Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2015.

raw.Explanation: A gastrinoma causes marked hypergastrinemia and gastric acid hypersecretion with treatment-refractory/atypical peptic ulcers and diarrhea; ~25% of cases occur within MEN1. Fasting gastrin must be interpreted with gastric pH (<2).

raw.Explanation: Biallelic ATP7B defects impair hepatocyte copper export, causing low serum ceruloplasmin, elevated 24-hour urinary copper, and corneal copper deposition (Kayser-Fleischer rings).

raw.Connection Title: Therapies that reduce copper burden in Wilson disease
raw.Explanation: Chelators (penicillamine, trientine) promote urinary copper excretion; zinc salts induce enterocyte metallothionein to block copper uptake; dietary restriction reduces intake. All lower body copper burden.
raw.Source Section: Liver / Wilson Disease; PDF pp. 65
raw.Notes: Different roles/mechanisms; category does not imply interchangeability or simultaneous use. Verified against AASLD Wilson Disease Practice Guidance 2022.

raw.Connection Title: Measures used to remove/reduce excess iron

raw.Connection Title: Markers of impaired synthetic/metabolic function in advanced cirrhosis

raw.Notes: Qualifier: PT/INR reflects synthetic function, not net bleeding risk in cirrhosis (rebalanced hemostasis); not all abnormalities are present simultaneously. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed.

raw.Notes: Do not claim a uniformly elevated HVPG: HVPG is normal in prehepatic and presinusoidal causes. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed.

raw.Connection Title: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia from reduced UGT1A1 conjugation

raw.Connection Title: Imaging and examination clues to acute cholecystitis
raw.Explanation: Cystic-duct obstruction and inflammation produce a positive Murphy sign, sonographic gallbladder wall thickening (>3 mm) and pericholecystic fluid, and nonvisualization of the gallbladder on HIDA (cholescintigraphy).
raw.Source Section: Biliary System / Acute Cholecystitis; PDF pp. 96
raw.Notes: Individual ultrasound signs are nonspecific; HIDA nonvisualization is sensitive but requires correct timing and has false positives. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed.

raw.Connection Title: Diagnostic pattern of chronic pancreatic exocrine insufficiency
raw.Explanation: Advanced chronic pancreatitis shows ductal calcifications and parenchymal atrophy with low fecal elastase (exocrine insufficiency), while normal D-xylose testing indicates intact small-bowel mucosal absorption - distinguishing pancreatic from mucosal malabsorption.
raw.Source Section: Pancreas / Chronic Pancreatitis; PDF pp. 127
raw.Notes: Normal D-xylose assumes no coexisting mucosal disease; calcifications and low elastase are not universal. Verified against Robbins & Cotran, 10th ed. and Yamada's Textbook of Gastroenterology, 7th ed.

raw.Connection Title: Fat-soluble vitamins at risk in pancreatic fat malabsorption
raw.Explanation: Pancreatic exocrine insufficiency impairs luminal fat digestion and micelle formation, reducing absorption of the four fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

raw.Notes: Fat-soluble vitamins (ADEK) is the equivalent accepted category name (not a competing category). Verified against Yamada's Textbook of Gastroenterology, 7th ed. (Vitamins and minerals).

raw.Connection Title: Orotic aciduria from UMP synthase deficiency
raw.Explanation: Hereditary orotic aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency) causes orotic acid accumulation, megaloblastic anemia unresponsive to B12/folate, and failure to thrive. Ammonia is normal, which distinguishes it from OTC deficiency, where orotic aciduria is accompanied by hyperammonemia.

Normal ammonia is a lab discriminator, not a symptom.

content.sourceSection: PDF p. 30 | Southern, Western, Northern Blot
content.notes: Method-target pairs verified (standard laboratory medicine). Caution: the paired-tile format reveals part of the association and may suit a learning mode over a competitive board.

raw.Notes: Consistent with NF1 diagnostic criteria (NIH/standard references; MedlinePlus Genetics). Keep the type 1 qualifier; pheochromocytoma is an associated complication, not universal.

raw.Explanation: Prader-Willi syndrome (loss of paternally expressed 15q11-q13) classically presents with neonatal hypotonia and poor feeding, followed in early childhood by hyperphagia, obesity, and hypogonadism. Features are age-dependent, not concurrent at birth.
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 40 | Disorders of Imprinting > Prader-Willi Syndrome
raw.Notes: Consistent with GeneReviews (Prader-Willi Syndrome) and MedlinePlus. Preserve age-dependent course: hypotonia is neonatal; hyperphagia/obesity emerge later.

raw.Explanation: Angelman syndrome (loss of maternally expressed UBE3A) features a happy demeanor with frequent laughter, seizures, ataxic gait, and intellectual disability with severe speech impairment.

raw.Notes: Consistent with GeneReviews (Angelman Syndrome) and MedlinePlus. UBE3A imprinting is tissue-specific (brain); laughter is a characteristic behavior, not a diagnostic requirement.

raw.Explanation: CF affects multiple digestive sites: pancreatic exocrine insufficiency (~80%) causing malabsorption and fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) vitamin deficiency, neonatal meconium ileus, and focal biliary cirrhosis/CF liver disease.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: GI and hepatobiliary manifestations of CF
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 41 | Key Mutations > Cystic Fibrosis
raw.Notes: Verified (Grasemann & Ratjen, NEJM 2023; CF Foundation hepatobiliary consensus, Sellers et al. 2024). Meconium ileus is neonatal; advanced/biliary cirrhosis affects only ~5-10%. Possible, not inevitable.

raw.Connection Title: Respiratory and related findings in cystic fibrosis
raw.Explanation: Defective CFTR-mediated airway surface hydration produces thick secretions, recurrent/chronic pulmonary infections, nasal polyps, and digital clubbing from chronic lung disease.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Pulmonary and upper airway CF findings
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 41 | Key Mutations > Cystic Fibrosis
raw.Notes: Consistent with Grasemann & Ratjen, NEJM 2023. Clubbing and recurrent infections are nonspecific (shared with other chronic suppurative lung diseases); the four-tile combination with nasal polyps improves specificity. Board overlap check advised.

raw.Connection Title: Vaso-occlusive complications of sickle cell disease
raw.Explanation: Vaso-occlusion drives dactylitis, acute chest syndrome, avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis), and ischemic stroke in sickle cell disease. Acute chest syndrome is multifactorial (infection, fat embolism, infarction), so this is an association with vaso-occlusion rather than an exclusive cause.
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 41 | Key Mutations > Sickle Cell Anemia
raw.Notes: Verified (Ware et al., Lancet 2017; Piel et al., NEJM 2017). Acute chest syndrome and stroke are not single-mechanism; keep association wording.

raw.Connection Title: Additional classic sickle cell disease complications
raw.Explanation: Sickle cell disease is associated with parvovirus B19-triggered transient aplastic crisis, functional autosplenectomy from repeated splenic infarction, Salmonella (and S. aureus) osteomyelitis, and renal papillary necrosis.
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 41 | Key Mutations > Sickle Cell Anemia
raw.Notes: Verified: Salmonella is a characteristic (not exclusive) cause of osteomyelitis in SCD, with S. aureus also common (Kao et al., Pediatr Blood Cancer 2020; NEJM Case 37-2023). Papillary necrosis and autosplenectomy confirmed (Ware et al., Lancet 2017). Associations, not universal findings.

raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Classic Duchenne findings; Childhood DMD presentation
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 42 | Muscular Dystrophies > Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
raw.Notes: Consistent with GeneReviews (Dystrophinopathies) and MedlinePlus. First three features overlap with other myopathies; early onset (<5 y) improves specificity but onset varies. Keep the age qualifier.

raw.Source Section: PDF pp. 42-43 | Myotonic Dystrophy

raw.Explanation: Frataxin deficiency causes degeneration/hypoplasia of the dorsal root ganglia and dorsal (posterior) columns, spinocerebellar tracts, and lateral corticospinal tracts (with dentate nucleus involvement). The category spans both sensory ganglia and spinal tracts.
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 43 | Friedreich Ataxia > Degeneration
raw.Notes: Sites verified (Indelicato et al., Nat Rev Neurol 2025; Harding et al., Ann Neurol 2021; Santos et al., Antioxid Redox Signal 2010; Scott et al., CNS Drugs 2024). Dorsal root ganglia are sensory ganglia, not a spinal cord tract - do not retitle as 'four spinal cord tracts.'

raw.Connection Title: Huntington disease psychiatric and motor presentation
raw.Explanation: Huntington disease (CAG/HTT) combines psychiatric features (depression, irritability/aggression), early hyperkinetic chorea, and later hypokinetic/rigid parkinsonism. Motor features are stage-dependent.
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 43 | Trinucleotide Repeat Expansion Diseases > Huntington Disease
raw.Notes: Consistent with GeneReviews (Huntington Disease). Early chorea and late hypokinesia reflect different disease stages and need not coexist; psychiatric features vary. Keep stage qualifiers.

raw.Connection Title: Williams syndrome cardiovascular and metabolic associations
raw.Explanation: Williams syndrome (7q11.23 deletion including ELN) causes an elastin arteriopathy with supravalvular aortic stenosis and other arterial stenoses (e.g., renal artery), plus idiopathic hypercalcemia (~15-45%). The ELN deletion underlies the vascular phenotype; the other tiles are clinical associations.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Williams syndrome clues; Elastin-deletion syndrome associations
raw.Source Section: PDF p. 45 | Microdeletion Syndromes > Williams Syndrome
raw.Notes: Verified (Morris & Braddock, AAP Williams syndrome guideline 2020; Kozel et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers 2021; MedlinePlus). ELN deletion explains the arteriopathy (SVAS, renal/other arterial stenoses); hypercalcemia mechanism is distinct and not universal. Mixing a genetic lesion with clinical findings is intentional and medically coherent.

raw.Explanation: Each blocks platelet ADP signaling through P2Y12, reducing platelet activation and aggregation.
raw.Source Section: Platelets - Antiplatelet Medications; PDF p. 51
raw.Notes: All four are P2Y12/ADP-receptor antagonists. Clopidogrel, prasugrel and ticlopidine are thienopyridine prodrugs; ticagrelor is a direct, reversible non-thienopyridine. Do not call all four irreversible. Ticlopidine is legacy (neutropenia/TTP). Ref: Goodman & Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 14th ed.

raw.Connection Title: Drugs associated with immune hemolytic anemia
raw.Explanation: These drugs can cause immune-mediated red-cell destruction through differing antibody mechanisms.
raw.Source Section: Normocytic Anemia - Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia; PDF p. 34

raw.Connection Title: Drugs inhibiting IL-2 production or signaling
raw.Explanation: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus reduce IL-2 transcription through calcineurin inhibition; sirolimus inhibits mTOR downstream of IL-2 signaling, and basiliximab blocks CD25, the IL-2 receptor alpha chain.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Inhibitors along the IL-2 activation pathway
raw.Source Section: Transplant Rejection - immunosuppressive pharmacology; PDF p. 76

Category correctly spans IL-2 production and signaling, not calcineurin alone.

raw.Connection Title: Pediatric hip disorders that can present with referred knee pain
raw.Explanation: Hip pathology commonly refers pain to the thigh or knee via the obturator nerve, so knee symptoms warrant hip examination. SCFE presents with knee or distal-thigh pain in roughly a quarter of cases, and Legg-Calve-Perthes classically refers pain to the knee.
raw.Accepted Alternate Category Names: Hip pathology presenting as knee pain

raw.Notes: REVISED: original tile 'Developmental hip dysplasia' replaced with 'Transient synovitis of the hip.' Infant DDH is clinically silent/painless and is detected by Ortolani/limited abduction, not knee pain (AAP DDH clinical report, Shaw & Segal, Pediatrics 2016; Singh et al., JAMA 2024 Rational Clinical Examination). Referred knee pain is best documented for SCFE (Webb et al., Am Fam Physician 2025; Karkenny et al., Pediatrics in Review 2018) and Perthes; transient synovitis is a common pediatric hip condition that presents with hip/limp and thigh-knee discomfort (de Borja et al., Curr Rev Musculoskelet Med 2022). Board note: referred knee pain is strongest for SCFE and Perthes; hip dislocation fits the general referred-pain principle but is less distinctive.

raw.Connection Title: Ocular and bulbar myasthenia gravis symptoms
raw.Explanation: Fatigable weakness of extraocular, eyelid, and bulbar muscles produces these symptoms in myasthenia gravis, typically with preserved pupillary function.
raw.Source Section: Neuromuscular Junction; PDF pp. 89
raw.Notes: These oculobulbar symptoms also occur in botulism, LEMS, and other neuromuscular disorders. Explanation should retain fatigability and pupil sparing. Avoid competing oculobulbar categories (botulism) on the same board.

raw.Explanation: LEMS impairs presynaptic acetylcholine release via P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium-channel autoimmunity; brief exercise transiently facilitates strength and reflexes, and roughly half of cases are paraneoplastic (most often SCLC).
raw.Source Section: Neuromuscular Junction; PDF pp. 90, 93
raw.Notes: SCLC is present in ~50-60% of cases (association, not required for diagnosis). Facilitation is with brief/short exercise, not sustained exertion. Verified: El-Wahsh & Reddel, Int Rev Neurobiol 2025; Punga et al., Lancet Neurol 2022; Maddison et al., Sci Rep 2020.

raw.Explanation: A complete oculomotor palsy impairs eyelid elevation and most extraocular muscles; parasympathetic involvement produces mydriasis and a 'down-and-out' eye.
raw.Source Section: Cranial Nerves I-VI; PDF pp. 98-99
raw.Notes: Pupillary dilation depends on parasympathetic fiber involvement; ischemic (e.g., diabetic) palsies classically spare the pupil. This set is specifically a complete, pupil-involving palsy (e.g., compressive/PCom aneurysm).

raw.Connection Title: Structures passing through the superior orbital fissure
raw.Explanation: CN III, IV, VI, and the ophthalmic division (V1) of the trigeminal nerve all enter the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.

raw.Connection Title: Branch-dependent effects of proximal facial nerve injury
raw.Tile 2: Loss of anterior two-thirds tongue taste

raw.Source Section: Cranial Nerves VII-XII; PDF pp. 106
raw.Notes: All four require a lesion proximal to the relevant branch points (at/above the geniculate region). A distal parotid-region motor lesion does not explain taste, lacrimation, or stapedius deficits. Verified: Gilden, NEJM 2004; ACR Appropriateness Criteria Cranial Neuropathy 2022.

raw.Connection Title: Retrochiasmal sites causing homonymous visual field loss
raw.Explanation: Unilateral lesions posterior to the optic chiasm disrupt corresponding portions of the contralateral visual field in both eyes (homonymous defects).
raw.Source Section: Vision; PDF pp. 119-121
raw.Notes: Pattern varies by site/extent: partial radiation lesions cause quadrantanopia (temporal=superior/Meyer loop; parietal=inferior). Macular sparing is possible, not obligatory, with occipital infarction.

raw.Explanation: Medulloblastoma is an aggressive embryonal cerebellar tumor that may show primitive small round blue cells and Homer-Wright rosettes and disseminate through the CSF.

raw.Notes: Do not require a vermian location for every molecular subgroup (WNT/SHH/group 3/group 4 differ in site). Homer-Wright rosettes are characteristic but not unique (also neuroblastoma).

raw.Explanation: Meningiomas arise from arachnoid cap cells and form extra-axial masses with whorled architecture and frequently laminated calcifications (psammoma bodies).

raw.Explanation: Ischemic brain injury may result from local large-vessel thrombosis, embolic obstruction, small penetrating-vessel disease, or global systemic hypoperfusion (watershed).

raw.Notes: These are mechanisms, which are not always mutually exclusive etiologic categories (cf. TOAST classification). Clean board-relevant set.

raw.Explanation: Alzheimer pathology features extracellular amyloid-beta plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles made of hyperphosphorylated tau; vascular amyloid deposition (CAA) commonly coexists.
raw.Source Section: Dementia; PDF pp. 204
raw.Notes: PARTIAL REDUNDANCY: hyperphosphorylated tau is the constituent protein of neurofibrillary tangles, so tiles 2 and 3 are closely linked (structure vs molecule) - retain as distinct teaching points but flag redundancy on a board. CAA can also occur independently. Verified: Kim et al., J Alzheimers Dis 2026; Barthelemy et al., Nat Med 2020.

raw.Explanation: Three cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine) and an NMDA-receptor antagonist (memantine) are used for symptomatic treatment of Alzheimer dementia.
raw.Source Section: Dementia; PDF pp. 204

raw.Connection Title: Potentially treatable contributors to cognitive impairment
raw.Explanation: These are potentially treatable conditions that can contribute to or mimic a dementia presentation and should be screened for in cognitive decline.
raw.Source Section: Dementia; PDF pp. 210
raw.Notes: Depression-related cognitive impairment is a reversible mimic; established neurologic injury from B12 deficiency or neurosyphilis may not fully reverse. Avoid the blanket label 'fully reversible dementias.'

raw.Connection Title: Cluster headache ipsilateral cranial autonomic signs
raw.Explanation: Cluster headache activates ipsilateral cranial autonomic/trigeminal-autonomic pathways, producing tearing, rhinorrhea, nasal congestion, and a partial Horner (miosis/ptosis).
raw.Source Section: Headache; PDF pp. 215
raw.Notes: These autonomic features are shared by all trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias (paroxysmal hemicrania, SUNCT), so they are not cluster-specific; avoid a competing TAC category on the same board. Attack duration/frequency distinguishes the TACs.

raw.Explanation: All four are phase II conjugation reactions that attach an endogenous polar group (glucuronic acid, acetyl, sulfate, or methyl) to a substrate; conjugation increases polarity but does not invariably inactivate the drug.

raw.Notes: All four verified as classic CYP inducers across CYP3A4/2C9/2C19 (Camilleri, Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019, Table 2; Song et al., Clin Pharmacokinet 2021, Table 1). Keep the one-or-more-enzymes wording given cimetidine is comparatively weak.

raw.Connection Title: Peripheral muscarinic findings in organophosphate (cholinergic) poisoning
raw.Explanation: Excess acetylcholine at peripheral muscarinic receptors produces these findings; nicotinic effects (fasciculations, weakness) and central effects (seizures) are separate categories.
raw.Source Section: Autonomic System > Anticholinesterase Poisoning, p. 30
raw.Notes: Verified muscarinic toxidrome features (Roberts et al., Nat Rev Dis Primers 2026; Henretig et al., NEJM 2019; Lavonas et al., AHA 2023; Cao et al., AHA 2025). Direct muscarinic-agonist excess reproduces the same quartet, so a general muscarinic-toxicity label is accepted. BOARD OVERLAP: each sign individually appears in other toxidromes.

raw.Connection Title: Benzodiazepines with oxidative phase I metabolism
raw.Explanation: These benzodiazepines undergo oxidative (CYP450 phase I) metabolism before conjugation, distinguishing them from the lorazepam-oxazepam-temazepam group that is cleared by glucuronidation alone.
raw.Source Section: Substance Misuse / Benzodiazepines; PDF p. 61
raw.Notes: Confirmed: alprazolam/midazolam/diazepam/chlordiazepoxide are CYP3A4/2C19 substrates while lorazepam/oxazepam/temazepam use UGT glucuronidation only (Smolders et al., Clin Pharmacokinet 2016; Gronich, Drugs Aging 2024; Prince et al., Drugs 2023). Do not imply identical half-lives or metabolite profiles.

raw.Explanation: NMS classically combines hyperthermia, marked (lead-pipe) rigidity, altered mental status, and autonomic instability after dopamine blockade.
